newsitem.title: UK: Outlook - Coffee rally grabs attention before talks.
newsitem.headline: Outlook - Coffee rally grabs attention before talks.

text.p: Coffee futures, already at record highs, should steal most of the limelight on London's soft commodity markets this week as producers hold a key meeting on exports, traders and analysts said.

Other markets were expected to be subdued by comparison, with sterling's strength against the dollar making gains difficult in London cocoa and with an industry function in New York sidelining major players in sugar.
Jitters over the fast-approaching Brazilian frost season could help sustain last week's dizzying rally on the London and New York coffee markets.
Roasters have warned that if prices stay at current levels consumption could fall by up to 10 million bags a year on a global basis.
Fund buying and spill-over arabicas sentiment drove July robustas to a high of $2,060 a tonne on Friday, a level not seen since late January 1996 and a 15-1/2 month peak.
July then rose further on Monday morning to hit $2,190 before edging back.
The arabicas market soared to 20-year highs basis May on Thursday on frantic buying by speculators and by commercial firms worried about low reserves and poor crop prospects.
But Friday saw a a downturn in sentiment as nervous players took profits and after New York's Green Coffee Association reported an increase in green coffee stocks.
Trade funds have held massive long positions in the robustas market since the frenzied buying from early January that has triggered the current five-month rally.

This week attention will focus on talks in London on Monday and Wednesday held by the Association of Coffee Exporting Countries (ACPC) to consider the future of its export quota programme beyond June.
The grouping could agree to defer plans to extend export quotas that were designed to keep a floor under world prices when they sagged last year.
Traders said they would continue to monitor weather conditions in Brazil as the frost season approaches.
But according to independent forecaster WSC, favourable conditions for coffee trees and Brazil's crop should continue with no cold weather threat in sight.
In cocoa, traders said the key July contract was likely to remain trapped between early April's range of 980 and 1,065 stg, despite what was seen by some as a promising upmove on Thursday.
But some traders remained positive, albeit slightly disappointed with Friday's performance.
"We still think it will go higher, but we might have to be patient," said one. "It could take some time."
They said sterling's continued strength against the U.S. dollar was making further gains difficult in London.
While July failed to test initial resistance around 1,038 stg on Friday, analysts said they would monitor the situation after July successfully filled a chart gap on Friday and closed at 1,016.

But if New York's equivalent July contract were to fill an overhead chart gap, fresh buying could emerge and drag London higher, while if London's July contract broke into the 1,060/65 area fund buying would be seen.
In white sugar, activity is expected to be subdued this week as players gather in New York for the Sugar Dinner on Wednesday.
Spot August is deriving support from Russian purchases of European white sugar, in addition to expected hefty arrivals of Brazilian and Cuban raws.
"The August is still going on the back of supposed Russian interest...but there's starting to be some support even further down the board," said one trader.
He noted increased interest at lower levels from end-users who had previously been deterred by high prices.
Some traders are believed to be putting white sugar into Russia and somehow avoiding the hefty 35 percent import and value-added tax. "Whether that can continue is debatable," the trader said.
Other market sources said suspected fund buyers were keeping August/October above $10 while scale-up producer selling was seen in August and October.
Speculators, normally more prevalent on the New York market, are also believed to have moved into August.
Traders said the unknown size of the spec position could cause August/October to widen towards expiry and then collapse during the bale-out in the last few days.
